extracted.intended_audience: attorneys admitted to practice before the USPTO, disciplinary counsel, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when a state disciplinary authority has disciplined an attorney; includes notice, response opportunity, factual standard, and publication/notification requirements. Applies to determining and announcing identical discipline (e.g., public reprimand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline based on discipline imposed by a duly constituted state authority; the USPTO Director (or delegated official) may enter orders such as public reprimand consistent with that state discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for imposing reciprocal discipline (predicate violation: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was publicly reprimanded for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being publicly reprimanded without terms from a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state disciplinary action (e.g., public reprimand) can serve as the predicate for a USPTO disciplinary finding under § 11.804(h); the Office treats such state discipline as a substantive basis for reciprocal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (certified mail; 40-day response period; Official Gazette publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' was sent by certified mail notifying Respondent and provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline. The Notice and Order was also published for two consecutive weeks in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural prerequisites include sending notice by certified mail, specifying the opportunity and deadline (40 days) to oppose, and publishing the Notice in the Official Gazette; failing to respond may result in default treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible defenses under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was given an opportunity to oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State Order based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the specific defenses are not enumerated on this page, the regulation § 11.24(d)(1) lists the limited bases on which a respondent may argue against reciprocal discipline; respondents must timely assert those statutory/regulatory defenses in their 40-day response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for decision — no genuine issue of material fact (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's public reprimand is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent does not timely contest the proceeding (or contest the factual predicates), the Office may find no genuine issue of material fact and impose the reciprocal discipline; timely contested factual/legal issues could prevent such a default finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline should mirror state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint requested that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline upon Respondent identical to the discipline imposed by the Order of the Fifth District, Section III Subcommittee of the Virginia State Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO aims to impose discipline identical to that imposed by the state (e.g., if the state publicly reprimanded without terms, the USPTO issues a public reprimand); the Office's order here is materially consistent with the state finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and publication of Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Public Reprimand' text, which summariz(es) the respondent, the violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), the underlying state order, and factual findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order supplies a model notice including required elements: respondent identity, authorization scope (trademark/non-patent matters, not authorized in patent matters), description of the state discipline, citation to the violated USPTO rule, factual summary (e.g., failure to deposit advanced fees into trust account), and reference to the state docket and order date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond Gazette publication, the OED must notify other jurisdictions' disciplinary agencies and courts where the attorney is admitted; these notifications communicate both the discipline and the factual/reasoning basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying ethical rule violated — Rule 1.15 Safekeeping of Property
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fifth District, Section III Subcommittee of the Virginia State Bar found that these acts constituted a violation of Rule 1.15 - Safekeeping of Property, which requires that advances for costs and expenses be deposited into a trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of misconduct supporting this finding include: representing a client, receiving an advanced legal fee ($650) and not depositing it into a trust account; acknowledgment that between Aug 2013 and Nov 2016 the attorney did not have a trust account and deposited client checks for expenses into his business account and paid expenses from the business account. Such conduct may support state discipline and thus reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final orders and disciplinary documents are publicly accessible via the OED FOIA reading room, supporting transparency and public notice of disciplinary outcomes.
